To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimum TS of PES for biogas production by rumen microorganism was 10% (wt), and the optimum biogas production reached 280.2 mL/g·TS, and the methane production reached 182.6 mL/g VS.
the methane production from paper sludge was enhanced by rumen microorganism, and the optimal feedstock concentration was 10% TS.
methane production from PES was enhanced by increasing the feedstock concentration, and the maximum methane production was obtained at 10 wt% of feedstock concentration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel methane production system and provides a new method for the treatment of PES.
a methane production system with rumen liquid as an inoculum, PES as a feedstock, and the effect of feed concentration on biogas production was studied.
the effect of feed stock concentration on methane production by inoculating rumen microorganisms in biomass solid waste.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methane production system with rumen microorganisms as inoculate microorganism and paper mill excess solid sludge as feedstock was feasible.
the biogas productivity and CH4 yield are significantly affected by the concentration of PES.
the optimal fermentation conditions were pH = 6.9, T = 39 ± 0.5 °C, slurry retention time = 20 days, and the sludge with total solid was 10 % in weight.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methane production system with rumen microorganisms as inoculate and PES as feedstock was feasible and efficient, which could be a new way of treating PES.
the methane yield of the PES is 182.7 L kg−1 VS, and it is higher than that of other biomass solid waste.
the biogas productivity was positively correlated with the input TS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rumen microorganisms have great potential for digesting the PES and the biogases produced can be used as fuel.
the biogas productivity and CH4 yield are significantly affected by the concentration of the feedstock.
a methane production system with a continuous stirred-tank reactor and rumen liquid as an inoculate microorganism can be used to digest PES.
